premise.claim: Issue sgl-project/rbg#284: "By turning on pprof, we could observe details and the reason is that irrelevant Pods consume most of the memory" — the rbg operator's informer cache retains every Pod in the cluster because cacheOptions() only filters Service/StatefulSet/Deployment by the group-name label.
premise.reportedComponent: operator informer cache (cmd/rbgs cacheOptions / controller-runtime cache)
premise.patchedComponent: design of the same cache (KEP-284 proposes the Pod admission rule); this PR is the KEP document only, implementation is TBD
premise.evidence: TestCacheOptionsConstrainsPodCache fails on the base code: cacheOptions() has 3 ByObject entries (Service, StatefulSet, Deployment) and none for *corev1.Pod, so the Pod informer is unfiltered — see results/unit-head.txt

findings.note: Guard tests: they PASS on base and head by design (they pin the label-selector semantics the KEP builds on). They are not bug repros; treat FIXED here as "semantics unchanged". A flip means the vendored client-go changed selector semantics.

liveNote: No live layer: the PR is a design document (keps/284-pod-cache-filter/**) and changes no runtime code, so there is nothing to exercise against a cluster in this round. When the implementation PR lands, graft this harness onto it: F1's contract tests must be green (either the implementation extends FilterSystemLabels/objects-meta comparison to ignore rbg.workloads.x-k8s.io/managed, or the KEP stops putting the marker into workload pod templates), and TestCacheOptionsConstrainsPodCache must be green (a Pod filter exists).
